caseStudies.title: Scribbles and Ink
caseStudies.summary: Two drawing games for PBS KIDS, with a different engineering challenge in each release.
caseStudies.challenge: In and Out had to run across a wide range of devices. Far and Away needed to make it easier for artists to create more content.
caseStudies.contribution: For In and Out, I worked around the engine editor's asset serialization constraints so we could load assets dynamically and manage memory at runtime. For Far and Away, we rewrote the original codebase around reusable behaviors and built editor tools so artists could add content themselves.
caseStudies.outcome: Both games shipped. I set up Google Analytics for Far and Away and used it to report to PBS KIDS on how the game was being played.

caseStudies.title: Global Mechanic's animation pipeline
caseStudies.summary: Internal production tools for a small animation studio.
caseStudies.challenge: The tools had to fit the production workflows of artists and producers, whose day-to-day technical needs I also supported.
caseStudies.contribution: I led the design of successive versions of the studio's full-stack animation pipeline tools. It was my largest ongoing development project there.

caseStudies.title: after-effects
caseStudies.summary: An open-source Node.js library for scripting Adobe After Effects.
caseStudies.challenge: Automating renders at SoMedia meant working with the older JavaScript engine inside After Effects. It runs separately from Node.js, with its own runtime state.
caseStudies.contribution: I packaged a bridge that sends JavaScript functions to After Effects and exchanges JSON-compatible arguments and results. The library supports synchronous calls and asynchronous calls that return promises.
caseStudies.outcome: Publishing the library led to contract work.

paragraphs: I learned to program as an animator. Writing expressions let me automate some of the motion I'd been setting up by hand. I still like finding the part of a creative workflow where a little code can save someone a lot of fiddling.
I like a clean abstraction, and I've lost enough time chasing one to know what it costs. There's always another way to structure the code, and there is, inconveniently, a deadline.
